text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0023"
description = "`RequestEvidenceDigest::matches_labeled` returning true means this handle names the profile's digest algorithm and its value IS the labeled digest of those bytes under that role's label."
justification = """
The replacement for ASM-0022, and deliberately much narrower: it constrains one three-line
comparator instead of leaving a twenty-line role-checking function meaningless.

What it does NOT assume is the important half. The digest is an UNINTERPRETED function of
`(label, bytes)` — nothing about SHA-256 is claimed, not collision resistance, not preimage
resistance, not even injectivity. Only functionality: the same label over the same bytes
gives the same value.

That is exactly enough to prove the binding DISCIPLINE — that each handle is checked under
its own required role label — and deliberately not enough to prove role SEPARATION, which
would need `label_a != label_b ==> digest(label_a, x) != digest(label_b, y)`. That is a
domain-separation property of the construction, it lives at
`boundary.crypto_primitives`, and no wording here should let it be read as proved.

The algorithm clause is a plain equality against the profile's single digest algorithm
identifier; it is trusted with the rest of the comparator.
"""
scope = ["unit://http_profile.continuation_binding", "boundary://boundary.unmodelled_own_behaviour"]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "ADR-MCPRE-059 WP3"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to `RequestEvidenceDigest::matches_labeled` or to its trusted Verus specification."
premise_class = "review-obligation"
discharging_event = { kind = "owner-event", statement = "`RequestEvidenceDigest::matches_labeled` is proved, with the labeled digest left uninterpreted, to satisfy its comparator contract: a true answer implies the handle names the profile's digest algorithm and its digest value equals labeled_digest(label, bytes). No property of the digest construction is claimed." }
affected_contracts = ["contract://http_profile/block/continuation_verify"]
sites = [
  "mcp-re-http-profile/src/evidence/digest.rs#RequestEvidenceDigest::matches_labeled",
]
tool_specific_mechanism = "verus:external_body"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0079"
description = "`Instant` is monotonic and advances at true rate while the process runs."
justification = """
A reload is due a cadence after the last one, measured on `std::time::Instant`; a cached key's
authority ends at its first-caching reading of the cache's clock plus the window `T` (THM-0097),
and that clock is `Instant`-elapsed seconds plus the highest wall-minus-monotonic offset seen, so
it advances at least as fast as `Instant` and a wall-clock step can only shorten `T`. Those are
DURATIONS, which is why they are not read off the wall clock — and a duration means something only
if the monotonic clock never goes back and advances at the rate time does. A clock that stalls keeps a cached answer authoritative past
`T`; that is the failure that matters here.

It is not a wall-clock premise and is not implied by one: a monotonic clock is trusted to
advance, not to agree with any peer.

It stops being acceptable if the reload cadence is measured on anything but the monotonic clock, or
if the cache's clock is built on anything that can advance slower than it.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://proxy.trust_resolution_window",
  "unit://proxy.trust_reload_cadence",
  "unit://proxy.admission_currency_gate",
  "boundary://boundary.monotonic_clock",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 RERE-RATIFICATION §4b P-4 (Ruling 40 step 4)"
review_requirement = "Owner review if a trust-plane window or cadence is measured on anything but `Instant`."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The host operating system's monotonic clock, across `std::time::Instant::now()`: successive
readings never decrease, and their differences track elapsed real time while the process runs.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0083"
description = "When `serde_json::from_slice` succeeds on a byte string into a `Value`, the byte string is an RFC 8259 JSON text, and for a text with no duplicate object member name the returned `Value` holds the object, array and scalar values that text encodes. When `serde_json::from_slice` succeeds on a byte string into the trust document's `Vec<RawEntry>` (`mcp-re-proxy/src/trust_document.rs`), the byte string is an RFC 8259 JSON text, and each named field of each `RawEntry` (`signer`, `key_id`, `public_key`, `slots`) holds the JSON member value from which it was deserialized."
justification = """
THM-0083 refuses a body unless it is a legal JSON-RPC 2.0 request, and establishes the
outstanding id from that one validation. Every clause after the first reads the body through
`serde_json::from_slice::<Value>`. The FIRST clause is this project's and is not part of this
premise: `reject_unrepresentable_json` refuses a duplicate member name, on the decoded form
`serde_json` keys on, before `serde_json` is asked anything — because `serde_json` resolves a
duplicate to one winner. What remains trusted is one direction only: when the parse succeeds,
the body was a JSON text, and for a text with no duplicate the `Value` returned represents the
objects, arrays and scalars the text encodes. It is not trusted that every RFC 8259 text is
accepted: a refusal of a legal text is a refusal, which the envelope's clauses treat as one.

The operator's trust document is read through the typed form, `serde_json::from_slice` into
`Vec<RawEntry>` (THM-0098), and only that one type: it relies on the same soundness fact, together
with fidelity for that representation. A document the parse accepts is a JSON text, and the
strings and values placed in `signer`, `key_id`, `public_key` and `slots` are the ones the text
wrote for those members, which is what binds each key id to the signer that wrote it. Nothing is
claimed for any other type that derives `serde::Deserialize`. The refusals of a member written
twice, of an unknown member, of an unknown slot and of `slots` that is not an array are this
project's, pinned by its own tests
(`a_duplicated_member_is_refused_rather_than_read_last_wins`,
`an_unknown_member_is_refused_rather_than_ignored`, `an_unknown_slot_is_refused_rather_than_ignored`,
`slots_must_be_an_array_when_present`); they are not part of this premise.

It stops being acceptable if the request envelope is read through another parser, or if the
representability check stops running first.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://http_profile.request_envelope",
  "unit://proxy.trust_document_interpretation",
  "boundary://boundary.json_parser",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 RERE-RATIFICATION §4b P-8 (Ruling 40 step 4)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the JSON parsing dependency, or to the order in which the envelope's clauses are asked."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The `serde_json` crate, across `from_slice` on a byte string. Into a `Value`: when it succeeds, the byte
string is an RFC 8259 JSON text, and for a text without duplicate member names the returned `Value`
holds the object, array and scalar values the text encodes. Into the trust document's
`Vec<RawEntry>`: when it succeeds, the byte string is an RFC 8259 JSON text, and each named field of
each `RawEntry` holds the JSON member value from which it was deserialized. It does not promise to
accept every RFC 8259 text, and nothing is claimed for any other type.
"""

tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0085"
description = "When MCP-RE decodes input through `ciborium` as a CBOR value, or through `coset` as a COSE_Sign1, and the decode succeeds, the decoded CBOR values correspond to the values the input bytes encode, and the decoded protected headers, unprotected headers, payload and signature are those the input bytes represent, with the protected and unprotected headers kept distinct. The `Sig_structure` that `coset` builds from such a decoded COSE_Sign1 for a signature check is the RFC 9052 section 4.4 encoding over the protected-header bytes exactly as received, and the external AAD and payload passed to it."
justification = """
THM-0041 reads a Signed Statement and a Receipt off the wire through `coset::CoseSign1` and
`ciborium`, and then reasons about what is in them: the algorithm and the claims it reads come
from the PROTECTED header, a receipt's position commitment comes from the protected header, and
its inclusion proof from the unprotected one. That the decoded structure is the one the bytes
encode, with the two headers not mixed, is the libraries' and nothing here establishes it.

The second sentence is for one conjunct: the Signed Statement's own COSE `Sig_structure` verified
under a key resolved for its issuer kid, and the same for the receipt's signature. MCP-RE does not
construct those signed bytes. `verify_cose_sign1_with_payload` hands `coset` a verifier callback and
`CoseSign1::verify_signature` / `verify_detached_signature` build the `Sig_structure` that is passed
to it. MCP-RE chooses the key, the algorithm check (`require_alg`) and, for a detached receipt, the
payload it re-derived.

Every refusal MCP-RE owns is NOT in this premise and is tested here: a non-empty or unknown `crit`,
an `iss` that is not the signing `kid`, a second occurrence of a CWT claim, trailing octets after
the statement's payload and after an inclusion proof, a repeated key in the `vdp` map, an unsupported
verifiable data structure, a leaf index outside the tree, and a root that is not a tree hash.

It stops being acceptable if SCITT evidence is decoded through another library, or if the signed
structure is ever built by this project instead of by `coset`.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_statement_attribution",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_receipt_shape",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_derived_root",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_algorithm_agreement",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_position_commitment",
  "boundary://boundary.cose_cbor",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 6 (owner ruling on the coset/ciborium premise)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the `coset` or `ciborium` dependency, or to how SCITT evidence is decoded or its signed structure is built."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The `ciborium` and `coset` crates, across a successful decode of CBOR input and of a COSE_Sign1,
and across the construction of the `Sig_structure` for a signature check from a decoded COSE_Sign1.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0086"
description = "`X509Certificate::verify_signature(None)` returns Ok only when the certificate signature verifies under the certificate's own subject public key."
justification = """
`credential_currency/x509_adapter` reports, for a certificate, whether it is self-signed: its
issuer `Name` encoding equals its subject `Name` encoding AND `verify_signature(None)` is Ok.
`evaluation` exempts a certificate reported self-signed from the validity-window check, so a
key-rollover intermediate (one that shares its name with its own issuer but is signed by another
key) is held to its window as path building holds it (THM-0032). Whether the exemption applies to
a given certificate therefore depends on `verify_signature(None)` answering Ok only for a signature
made under the certificate's own subject public key; the library's signature check is the
library's, and nothing here establishes it.

What stays this project's and is tested here: the comparison of the two `Name` encodings, the
conjunction of that comparison with the signature check, the exemption itself, and that the
validity window still applies to every certificate not reported self-signed
(`a_self_issued_certificate_is_self_signed_only_under_its_own_key`). This premise says nothing
about certificate trust, path validity, issuer selection or X.509 in general.

It stops being acceptable if the adapter checks a certificate's signature through another call,
or passes a key to `verify_signature` instead of `None`.
"""
scope = ["unit://proxy.credential_currency", "boundary://boundary.x509"]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 7 (owner ruling on THM-0032)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the credential-currency X.509 adapter, to its parser dependency, or to how a certificate is reported self-signed."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The pinned `x509_parser` crate, across `X509Certificate::verify_signature(None)`: it returns Ok
only when the certificate's signature verifies under the certificate's own subject public key.
"""

tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0087"
description = "When `napi` invokes an exported `#[napi]` function of the TypeScript native binding, each `Buffer`, string, number and array argument arrives as the JavaScript caller passed it, and the object the function returns, or the error it raises, reaches the caller with each member and message as the function produced it, a member left `None` arriving absent."
justification = """
THM-0095 says what an application is handed, and the application receives it through `napi`:
the request bytes the exchange transmitted go in as a `Buffer`, the caller's trust inputs go in as
strings, numbers and arrays, and the verdict comes back as an object. The binding does everything
it owns before and after that layer: it passes the received bytes to the audited core unchanged,
builds the anchor and policy from the received values, and fills `VerifyResultJs` field for field
with an execution member the receipt did not state left `None`. That the bytes it received are the
bytes the caller passed, and that the object it built is the object the caller reads, is `napi`'s.

What stays this project's and is tested here: the refusal of an empty issuer identity, the
refusal of a time that is not whole seconds, the judgement of a retired root at the caller's
`now`, and the projection (`an_absent_execution_member_stays_absent_in_the_projection`,
`a_rejection_is_not_reported_as_a_success`). This premise says nothing about the Node runtime,
about `napi` correctness in general, or about what the TypeScript layer does with the object.

It stops being acceptable if the binding converts a value itself before handing it to the core, or
returns a type whose conversion this premise does not cover.
"""
scope = ["unit://sdk_typescript.native_binding", "boundary://boundary.napi_marshalling"]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 7 (owner ruling on native marshalling)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the napi dependency, or to a type the binding takes or returns across the N-API boundary."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The pinned `napi` and `napi-derive` crates, across an exported `#[napi]` function: the `Buffer`,
string, number and array arguments arrive as passed, and the returned object or raised error
reaches the caller as produced, a member left `None` arriving absent.
"""

authority: Owner ruling, step 7 round 5 (2026-10-09): exact current theorem-entry bytes and digest in STEP7-R5-SIGNATURES.md approved
text:
[[theorem]]
id = "THM-0041"
title = "An offline-verified receipt proves registration, and its root was never supplied"
statement = """
If `verify_receipt_offline` returns Ok, then: the Signed Statement's own COSE
`Sig_structure` verified under a key resolved for its issuer kid, so the statement is
attributed to the party that actually signed it and to no other; the statement carries the
RFC 9943 §6.1 CWT claims in its PROTECTED header, with `iss` equal to the signing kid, `sub`
equal to the MCP-RE statement subject and the MCP-RE statement content type, so no other
`COSE_Sign1` the same key produces can be read as MCP-RE call evidence; the receipt parsed
as an RFC 9942 §5.2.1 receipt; running the RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2 inclusion algorithm over the
statement's leaf hash at the receipt's leaf index and tree size produced a root that, for an
ATTACHED receipt, equals the root the receipt commits to and, for a DETACHED one, IS the
payload the transparency-service signature was checked against; the transparency service's
signature verified under a key resolved for its kid; where the pinned profile binds the
position, the commitment the service SIGNED equals the one recomputed over that derived
root; and both signatures were attempted only under an algorithm the protected header names
and the resolved key agrees with, out of EdDSA and ES256 and nothing else. No network was
contacted.
"""
security_consequence = """
The root is DERIVED from the statement under verification and never supplied by the caller,
on either payload form. A receipt cannot be made to verify by handing in a convenient root,
and on the detached form a wrong fold produces a different `Sig_structure`, so the signature
simply fails rather than being compared against something the caller chose.

An auditor can therefore check that a record existed without trusting the log to replay
honestly and without contacting it. Attribution is part of that: possession of a parsed
`SignedStatement` proves nothing — `SignedStatement::from_cose` deliberately parses without
verifying — and it is THIS operation, over the exact signed bytes, that makes the issuer
claim true. Algorithm confusion is refused rather than attempted.
"""
direct_consequence_severity = "high"
scope = """
It establishes registration on A SERVICE whose key was resolved. It does NOT establish that
the service is honest, that its log is append-only, that the entry is unique, or anything
about the log's current state — this is offline verification, and none of those properties
is checkable without the log.

It does not judge the transparency-service key's lifecycle: a resolved key is used whatever its
validity window or revocation status. That a receipt's key was acceptable when the receipt was
accepted is the caller's, judged with `TransparencyKeyLifecycle::admits_at` at its trusted
current time, and is not established here.

It says nothing about the CALL the statement describes: that the retained evidence is the
evidence the statement was made about is THM-0042, a separate proposition over a separate
authority.

The two RFC 9162 implementations in this tree stay two on purpose. `prototype` builds a
tree and `merkle` verifies a path, and they are an independent cross-check; this claim is
over the verification side alone and must not be read as a claim about the builder.
`PrototypeTransparencyService` is a public compatibility surface, test/conformance support
and a build-side oracle, and is NOT a production security product — no consequence here
depends on it.

`ReceiptPositionProfile::Bound` is selected only by the pin's `position_profile`. The position
conjunct above holds exactly for `Bound`. `Bound` is exercised only against the prototype
transparency service.
"""
owner = "http_profile.scitt_derived_root"
review_requirement = "Owner security-specification review"
# ADR-MCPRE-068 Phase 1. THE SIX LEAVES BELONG HERE, not one altitude up. This claim IS the
# conjunction of what a successful `verify_receipt_offline` establishes, and
# `http_profile.scitt_receipt_offline` named all six in its own description while owning
# them as one. THM-0072 reaches them through its dependency on this claim and adds the one
# thing it does not say: that the resolver was PROJECTED FROM a pinned service document.
supported_by = [
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_statement_attribution",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_receipt_shape",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_inclusion_fold",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_derived_root",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_position_commitment",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_algorithm_agreement",
]
depends_on = []

authority: Owner ruling, step 7 round 5 (2026-10-09): exact current theorem-entry bytes and digest in STEP7-R5-SIGNATURES.md approved
text:
[[theorem]]
id = "THM-0063"
title = "A signed response never advertises validity its credential does not authorize"
statement = """
`SigningWindow` (in `mcp-re-http-profile`) keeps `expires` private and no constructor accepts
one: every window is derived as the earlier of the configured TTL from `now` and the
credential's own `exp`, with saturating arithmetic so an absurd configured TTL cannot wrap
past it. A credential already past its bound, or a non-positive TTL, obtains no signing
window at all, and with no window nothing is signed. The delegated signing key is
crate-private to its `ActiveDelegatedKey`, and the emitters that read it take a window, so a
signature under a delegated credential cannot advertise any other validity. The proxy opens
windows at two sites — the exchange's opener and a refusal that carries its exchange's
snapshot — and both go through `SigningWindow::over`; every window this deployment signs
under, reply and refusal alike, is opened at one of them, and a refusal signs under the
snapshot its own exchange took.
"""
security_consequence = """
A client cannot be given a receipt asserting validity beyond the moment its credential stops
authorizing signatures — a window the verifier refuses as soon as the credential's own closes,
which the client would learn about only by failing. And a refusal minted late in an exchange
cannot advertise more validity for having been reached by a different path.
"""
direct_consequence_severity = "high"
scope = """
The advertised window, not the signature. It does not establish that a credential existed
(THM-0062) or what the signature covers (THM-0065). Where no valid credential exists the
receipt is UNSIGNED, and what such a receipt may still state is a separate conjunct of this
unit rather than part of this claim.
"""
owner = "proxy.response_signing"
review_requirement = "Owner security-specification review"
supported_by = ["unit://proxy.response_signing", "unit://proxy.delegated_signing_credential", "unit://http_profile.delegated_signing_custody"]
depends_on = []

authority: Owner ruling, step 7 round 5 (2026-10-09): exact current theorem-entry bytes and digest in STEP7-R5-SIGNATURES.md approved
text:
[[theorem]]
id = "THM-0093"
title = "An answer leg that needs a continuation does not proceed unbound"
statement = """
Where a request carries a continuation, the retained open-leg evidence handles are read
WITHOUT being spent, and no way they can be absent yields a binding: the dispatcher fails closed rather than
admitting an unbound continuation.

The absences are ATTRIBUTED, not merely detected. A store that does not ANSWER, and a
deployment that holds no correlation capability while this leg needs one, are refused before
admission and named as facts about the DEPLOYMENT. Only the caller-side absences — the request
names no `requestState`, or the store answered and the entry was never opened, has expired, or
was already answered — leave no binding and let the leg be refused as the caller's.

The spend is the store's atomic consume and has four outcomes, because the store's error is
not its negative answer: nothing was at stake, this call spent the approval, the store
answered and there was nothing live to spend, or the store did not answer and whether the
entry is gone cannot be determined by anything downstream.
"""
security_consequence = """
A signed continuation that cannot be bound to a live approval is never admitted, so a second
verified actor cannot complete a human approval round trip that was not its own by presenting
a continuation the deployment cannot check. The read is free, so a request about to be refused
for an unrelated reason leaves a live approval intact — the refusals above the retirement stay
free only because nothing above them spent anything.

A deployment's own missing capability is never reported as the caller's forgery. Without that
conjunct the fail-closed behaviour is still safe and its diagnosis is false: every legitimate
answer leg reaching a deployment that selected no correlation store reads on the wire as a
splice attempt, and a genuine splice attempt is indistinguishable from an ordinary deployment
posture. An operator cannot act on either, and a defender cannot tell them apart.

The four-valued retirement preserves the observed fate of the approval without inventing
certainty: no approval was involved, this exchange spent it, the store answered and there was
nothing live to spend, or its fate is indeterminate. These are four different facts about a
person's decision, and they are carried forward so the exchange-lifecycle authority can derive
the consequence. THM-0093 does not decide retry policy and does not assert that any particular
retry will succeed; what it establishes is that the four facts reach that authority undistorted
rather than collapsed into one another.
"""
direct_consequence_severity = "critical"
scope = """
It is about what a leg may PROCEED on and how a request-time absence is ATTRIBUTED — never
about what the deployment was built or configured with. Which capability the runtime installs
for the plan it was given, and what the startup transcript says about it, is THM-0096's and is
deliberately not restated here. This claim observes its own `ContinuationPlane` state and
consumes no proposition from THM-0096, which is why no edge to it exists: both discuss
absence, and they establish different things.

It says nothing about the continuation binding check itself, which is
`mcp-re-http-profile`'s and is where a bound-but-wrong continuation is caught, and nothing
about what an acknowledged store write durably establishes.

The `Indeterminate` retirement is reported, not resolved. Nothing downstream can find out
whether the entry was consumed, and this claim does not pretend otherwise — what it
establishes is that the outcome is carried as its own case rather than collapsed into one of
the other three.
"""
owner = "proxy.continuation_leg_binding"
review_requirement = "Owner security-specification review"
supported_by = ["unit://proxy.continuation_leg_binding", "unit://proxy.continuation_consume_contract"]
depends_on = ["THM-0087"]

authority: Owner ruling, step 7 round 5 (2026-10-09): exact current theorem-entry bytes and digest in STEP7-R5-SIGNATURES.md approved
text:
[[theorem]]
id = "THM-0104"
title = "Shutdown stops admission and bounds the wait on admitted work; what the drain leaves behind it never resumes"
statement = """
For one core of the async serving path, from the moment a shutdown is signalled:

ADMISSION STOPS. The accept loop observes the shutdown signal within one accept-poll interval
and exits before the drain begins; a connection accepted inside that interval is counted and
drained like any other. The drain signal puts every connection that exists into graceful
shutdown: it finishes the requests it has, writes their responses, and admits no further
request on it, keep-alive or multiplexed alike.

ADMITTED WORK IS COUNTED UNTIL ITS CONNECTION ENDS. A connection is OPEN from an RAII guard
taken at accept, before its TLS handshake, until its connection task ends. The guard's
construction is the only increment and its `Drop` the only decrement, so a connection cannot
be served without being counted, nor counted after it has finished. The task lives until the
HTTP layer has finished the connection, which is after the last response it started has been
written and flushed, so the count is a count of connections not yet finished — never of
requests not yet started, and never of requests whose handler has merely returned. A reply
still being written holds the count above zero.

THE DRAIN WAITS ON THAT COUNT, BOUNDED. It signals the drain, then polls while the count is
non-zero and returns when the count reaches zero OR the grace deadline passes, whichever comes
first. A grace that cannot be turned into an instant makes the drain signal and then decline to
wait, rather than park process exit behind a deadline it cannot enforce.

WHAT THE GRACE LEAVES BEHIND MAY BE CANCELLED. When the drain returns, the core's runtime is
dropped and a task still suspended at an await point is cancelled there. That await point may
be anywhere a connection's processing suspends, INCLUDING INSIDE THE HANDLER and INSIDE THE
WRITE OF A REPLY: a reply the grace cut off is the grace's doing and nothing before it.

CANCELLATION IS TERMINAL. A task cancelled by the runtime drop is never polled again: it does
not enter the handler afterwards, and it does not resume inside it. Once `serve` returns, no
admitted request makes further progress — which is the fact teardown's second phase relies on
when it drops the trust, signing and TLS planes.
"""
security_consequence = """
An operator draining a replica — a rolling deploy, a scale-down, a node drain — gets two
facts, and must not be sold a third.

The two: nothing new is admitted once the accept loop has observed the signal, and no
admitted request executes, or
resumes executing, after `serve` returns, so the planes are dismantled behind work that has
provably stopped rather than work assumed to have stopped. Within the grace, a reply a
connection had started is delivered rather than cut off by the runtime drop.

The third, which this mechanism does NOT provide: that a request cancelled at grace expiry
had not already executed. The in-flight count does not distinguish a request stalled in its
body read from one suspended inside the handler, so once the grace expires the drain cannot
say on which side of the exchange's execution threshold the abandoned work sat.

Whether a client may safely retry an abandoned request is therefore decided by the exchange
state and retry authorities, on the evidence THOSE authorities hold about how far the exchange
progressed — never by the drain counter. A deployment wanting zero-abandoned drain in fact
rather than in bound configures `drain_grace >= request_deadline`; that is a configuration
relation resting on the request deadline's own enforcement, and is not claimed here.
"""
direct_consequence_severity = "medium"
scope = """
WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED, in terms, because an earlier statement of this theorem claimed all three
and was corrected by owner ruling on 2026-09-06: that a request which reached the handler runs
to completion and is answered; that every admitted request ends answered or never executed;
that retry of an abandoned request is safe because the handler was never entered. The
connection guard spans handshake, body read, handler and response writing alike, and the drain
exits on the grace as readily as on the count, so runtime teardown after grace expiry can cancel a task suspended
INSIDE `handler(..).await`. The battery's
`a_request_abandoned_by_the_grace_never_reaches_the_handler` exercises a request stalled in its
BODY READ; it establishes that cancellation is terminal for a task that had not yet reached the
handler, not that every abandoned task is such a task.

NOTHING HERE BOUNDS HOW LONG TEARDOWN TAKES. That an idle drain returns promptly, that a
saturated drain finishes within a few seconds, and that a stuck request cannot delay exit much
past the grace are WALL-CLOCK MEASUREMENTS taken on the box that ran them — real controls
(`idle_drain_returns_promptly`, `stuck_request_cannot_delay_exit_past_grace`, and the tail
assertions of the two zero-abandoned controls), part of the battery this unit's evidence rests
on, but not conjuncts of this claim. A red from one of them is a statement about the machine,
not about the property. The bounded-exit guarantee an operator configures (`drain_grace` under
a Kubernetes termination grace period) is that timing property and is therefore not claimed
here either.

ONE core, and the async path. The per-core fleet inherits the mechanism because each core's
`serve` drains before its worker thread joins, but that composition is not stated. The blocking
mTLS harness is not an MCP-RE serving path and is out of scope.

The cancellation half is STRUCTURAL — a task suspended at an await point when its runtime is
dropped is not polled again — and has no deletable check, so it carries no probe; what a probe
can reach is the drain's wait and the guard that makes the count move. The three non-UTF-8
header controls sharing this test binary belong to a boundary-refusal authority that has no
owner, and are not evidence for anything here.

Outside every root's closure, deliberately and for the same reason as THM-0012: no root's
dispatch or response claim rests on what shutdown does to work already admitted. Executable,
class V0, measured under the `async_serve` feature lane named by the owning unit.
"""
owner = "proxy.serving_drain"
review_requirement = "Owner security-specification review"
supported_by = ["unit://proxy.serving_drain"]
depends_on = []
